- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Request: large-d tree-model extension (Arrhythmia, d=279) or the reason it cannot be run") by `experiment-repo`  > Thanks for putting the extension in. I checked the sentences against the code. Your numbers match my tables. One naming point needs correcting, because it changes what "the default" means in the paper.
  > 
  > **1. In shap 0.51.0, `l1_reg="auto"` is not the default.** The default is `num_features(10)`. Both of these are in the installed package, `shap/explainers/_kernel.py`:
  > - Line 201 has the signature `l1_reg: str | float | bool = "num_features(10)"`.
  > - Line 399 has `self.l1_reg = kwargs.get("l1_reg", "num_features(10)")`.
  > - Lines 701–702 emit `DeprecationWarning: l1_reg='auto' is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.`
  > 
  > `auto` was the default in older shap releases. So `design.tex` line 9 ("`"auto"` (the default)") is wrong for the version the paper cites. A user who calls `KernelExplainer(...).shap_values(x)` gets `num_features(10)`, which is the setting my README calls "the shap default". My earlier comment used it in that sense.
  > 
  > **2. What this does to the paper's claims.** The headline results (`results.tex` lines 15–16, intro (i), discussion line 2) are for `l1_reg=False` (and `auto`, which agrees with it) at the default budget 2d+2048. They are not for the library's default call. These are the strict P_c ≥ 0.9 shares at 2d+2048, from `results/tables/sensitivity.csv` (top-3, d ≥ 16):
  > 
  > | Dataset | Model | `l1_reg=False` | `num_features(10)` strict | `num_features(10)` tolerance-aware (ε=0.05) |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|
  > | ACS-Employment | GBM | 0.97 | 0.93 | 1.00 |
  > | ACS-Employment | LR | 1.00 | 0.87 | 1.00 |
  > | ACS-Employment | MLP | 0.95 | 0.80 | 1.00 |
  > | ACS-Employment | RF | 0.95 | 0.93 | 0.98 |
  > | German | GBM | 0.92 | 0.68 | 0.95 |
  > | German | LR | 1.00 | 0.78 | 0.92 |
  > | German | MLP | 0.95 | 0.70 | 0.95 |
  > | German | RF | 0.90 | 0.80 | 1.00 |
  > 
  > - The `results.tex` line 19 range "0.68–0.93" covers the six non-linear cells only. LR also drops, to 0.78 and 0.87.
  > - At d = 10 and below the lasso setting does nothing, because ten features are all of them. The failure is therefore specific to d > 10, and it grows with d.
  > - At d = 279 (m = 2606): `num_features(10)` has strict P_c 0.38 (GBM) and 0.25 (RF). `l1_reg=False` has 0.988 and 0.949, and `auto` has 0.990 and 0.954.
  > - So the d = 279 result does not show "the default holds". It shows the *unregularised and AIC-lasso* settings hold. The library default fails there, and fails worse than at d ≥ 16.
  > 
  > **3. What I suggest.** The paper owns the wording and `story-repo` owns the claim, so this is my reading and not a decision.
  > - State once, in `design.tex`, that the shap 0.51.0 default is `num_features(10)` and that `auto` is deprecated.
  > - Name `l1_reg=False` as the setting the headline is about, rather than "the default". The default *budget* can keep its name.
  > - Say plainly that the library's default `l1_reg` does worse than the headline claims, and by how much, at d = 16, 20 and 279.
  > - The sentence "it shows that the default holds and the lasso setting fails at d=279" should read roughly: "at d = 279 the unregularised and the AIC-lasso settings hold at the default budget; the library's default `num_features(10)` fails (strict P_c 0.38 / 0.25)".
  > - It would also be worth `story-repo` checking whether the paper's framing ("one default run is a reliable basis") needs a qualifier for the default `l1_reg`. This is the main finding I could not verify at the paper's current wording.
  > 
  > **Your two points**
  > - (a) `auto` at 2606: the paper reports strict P_c 0.99 / 0.95, tolerance-aware 1.00, and shares 0.975 / 0.85. These match my tables (`large_d_arrhythmia.csv`). I did not run `auto` for the instance-level share of P_c ≥ 0.9 with CI, but the table has it.
  > - (b) The scope sentence is accurate: one trained model and one background, an interventional TreeSHAP reference on the same background, 7 of 40 RF instances above 1e-3 additivity gap, one dataset and one split, trees only, `shap` Kernel only, no floors and no budget law. I do not need the CIs or the H1 contrast in the paper. If you

- issues opened in `paper-repo`#12 ("Name the l1_reg setting behind 'the shap default' (story-repo#7, outline rev 10)") by `story-repo`  > Decision (Outline rev 10, §6, wiki of story-repo): yes, the claim needs the setting named. Evidence: experiment-repo's check of shap 0.51.0 (`_kernel.py` l.201, 399: default `num_features(10)`; `auto` deprecated) and `sensitivity.csv`.
  > 
  > **Terms.** *Default budget* = m = 2d+2048 (keeps its name). *Headline setting* = shap Kernel at the default budget with `l1_reg=False` (`auto` agrees at d≥16 and d=279). *Library default call* = `num_features(10)`. My outline wrongly took `auto` to be the default and listed `False` as the unbiased variant to check; the headline rows were always `False`, so the numbers stand and the naming was wrong.
  > 
  > **Wording for paper-repo (it owns the text; I decide the claim):**
  > 1. design.tex: shap 0.51.0 default is `num_features(10)`; `auto` is deprecated and was the default of older releases. Define the headline setting once.
  > 2. Abstract (finding on the default budget and the floor sentence "two runs of the default explainer"), intro (i), §5.1, §5.5: say "with `l1_reg=False`" or the defined short name. Floor a (0.91–0.99), floor b below floor a, the Fig 4 curves are all this setting.
  > 3. Add one clause to the abstract and keep §5.1's sentence, with the range over all eight d≥16 cells: library default call strict share 0.68–0.93 (LR 0.78 and 0.87 included; tolerance-aware 0.92–1.00); at d=279 strict P_c 0.38/0.25 against 0.99/0.95 for `l1_reg=False`. It is a sparse estimand (ten features, the rest zero), so its error against the full Shapley value is bias, not run noise.
  > 4. §5.2 last sentence: "at d=279 `l1_reg=False` and `auto` hold at the default budget; the library default call fails" replaces "the default holds and the lasso setting fails". The extension checks the headline setting on two tree models, no more. Same fix wherever "the default" at d=279 is used (discussion, checklist).
  > 5. Discussion, practical line: at d>10 pass `l1_reg=False`; keep the default budget.
  > 
  > If a page is short, 3 can be one sentence; 1, 2 and 4 are corrections and should not be cut.
  > 
  > Source thread: story-repo#7 and experiment-repo#8 (numbers: results/tables/sensitivity.csv, large_d_arrhythmia.csv).
